lessons.title: Part A of Form 16: The TDS Your Employer Deducted and Deposited

children.text: When Priya's Form 16 for FY 2025-26 lands in her inbox in June 2026, she does what most people do: scrolls straight to the tax figure at the end of Part B. That is a mistake. Part B is your employer's calculation. Part A is the evidence. It shows whether the tax cut from your salary actually reached the government against your PAN, and it takes about three minutes to check.

body.text: Part B tells you how much tax your employer thinks you owe. Part A tells you how much of it was actually deposited in your name. Only the second one becomes your tax credit.

children.text: The Header: Who, Whose PAN and Which Year
The top of Part A identifies the certificate, the employer, you and the year. Every field here has a job, and three of them can silently break your credit if they are wrong.

body.caption: Form 16 Part A header fields and what to check

Needed to verify the certificate online
Date the underlying TDS data was last processed
A recent date after a correction means the fix went through
Name and address of the Employer

body.text: If the PAN in Part A is wrong by even one character, your TDS has been credited to someone else, or to no one. Your return will show less tax paid than was actually deducted. Only your employer can fix this, by filing a correction statement, so raise it with HR the day you notice.

children.text: The Quarterly Summary
Below the header is a summary table with one row per quarter. It comes straight from the four quarterly TDS statements your employer filed, which were Form 24Q for FY 2025-26.
Receipt numbers of original quarterly statements:
The acknowledgement number of each quarterly statement. A blank here means that quarter was never filed.
Amount paid/credited:
Salary paid to you in that quarter, as reported by the employer.
Amount of tax deducted:
TDS cut from your salary that quarter.
Amount of tax deposited/remitted:
TDS actually paid to the government for you that quarter.
Here is what Priya's summary looks like. Her ₹18 lakh salary was paid evenly across the year, and her employer deducted ₹14,500 a month.

body.caption: Priya's Part A quarterly summary, FY 2025-26 (receipt numbers illustrative)

body.text: The two columns that matter most are tax deducted and tax deposited. They should be equal in every row. If tax deposited is lower, money was cut from your salary but has not reached the government against your PAN.

children.text: The Challan Details: Proof of Deposit
The last table in Part A lists how the money was paid into the government account, one row per deposit. Private employers deposit through a bank
challan
, so their table is titled details of tax deducted and deposited through challan. Government employers deposit through book adjustment and use a separate table instead.

markDefs.definition: The payment slip used to deposit tax with the government. Each challan is identified by the bank's BSR code, the date of deposit and a challan serial number.

children.text: Employers usually pay one challan each month covering all employees. The column
tax deposited in respect of the deductee
shows only your share of that challan.

body.caption: First three rows of Priya's challan table (bank details illustrative)

body.title: See all 12 deposits and the due dates they met

children.text: TDS deducted in any month must be deposited by the 7th of the following month. The one exception is March, which gets until 30 April.

body.latex: \sum_{q=1}^{4} \text{TDS deposited}_q \;=\; \sum_{m=1}^{12} \text{Challan deposit}_m \;=\; \text{Form 26AS credit against the employer's TAN}
body.caption: Three numbers that must agree: quarterly summary total, challan table total and Form 26AS

children.text: What the OLTAS Status Letters Mean
The last column of the challan table shows whether the department matched the employer's statement with the bank's record of payment in
OLTAS
. You will see one of four letters.

markDefs.definition: Online Tax Accounting System, the department's system that records tax payments received through banks.

cells: The deposit in the bank matches the employer's statement
Nothing. This is what you want to see.
Credit given on the statement alone, used for government deductors until the Pay and Accounts Office verifies it
Usually nothing. It normally turns to F after verification.
The employer has not deposited the tax, or quoted wrong challan details
Ask HR to check the challan details and file a correction.
The challan matched, but the employer claimed more against it than was actually deposited
Ask HR to either reduce the claim or deposit the shortfall.

children.text: Deducted but Not Deposited: Are You on the Hook?

Suppose your payslips show TDS every month, but Part A shows status U or a lower deposited amount. Legally, you are protected. Section 401 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (section 205 of the 1961 Act) says you cannot be asked to pay tax yourself to the extent it has already been deducted from your income. CBDT instructions issued in 2015 and 2016 tell assessing officers not to enforce demands that arise only because a deductor failed to deposit TDS.

In practice, though, the system processing your return only sees what is filed against your PAN. A missing credit can still trigger a demand notice that you then have to contest. The easiest path is to get the employer to fix it before you file, and to keep your payslips and appointment letter as evidence of the deduction.
Verify That Your Form 16 Is Genuine
Part A is generated through TRACES, so you can confirm it is genuine without logging in anywhere. TRACES has a public Verify TDS Certificate facility.

body.title: Your 3-minute Part A check
steps: Confirm the PAN of the Employee is exactly your PAN.
Confirm the Assessment Year is AY 2026-27 for salary earned in FY 2025-26, and the period matches your employment dates.
Check every quarter has a receipt number, and tax deducted equals tax deposited in each row.
Check every row in the challan table shows status F.
On TRACES, use Verify TDS Certificate with the employer's TAN, the certificate number, assessment year, source of income (salary) and the TDS amount.
Open Form 26AS and confirm the total against your employer's TAN matches the Part A total.

body.label: TRACES: Verify TDS Certificate
body.description: Use the Verify TDS Certificate option on the TRACES home page. No login is needed.

children.text: Check Your Understanding

body.title: Add up Rohan's Part A
body.prompt: Rohan works for an IT services firm in Hyderabad. His Part A shows tax deducted of ₹38,000 in Q1, ₹38,000 in Q2, ₹41,000 in Q3 and ₹45,000 in Q4. What total TDS credit should he expect in Form 26AS against his employer's TAN?
body.explanation: ₹38,000 + ₹38,000 + ₹41,000 + ₹45,000 = ₹1,62,000. TDS often rises later in the year as employers adjust for bonuses, increments or late investment proofs, so unequal quarters are normal.

body.title: Read the status
body.question: A row in the challan table of Part A shows status U. What does this most likely mean?
options: The deposit is final and matched
The employer has not deposited the tax, or quoted wrong challan details
The credit is provisional pending verification by a Pay and Accounts Office
The employer deposited more than it claimed
body.explanation: U means unmatched: the department could not find a bank deposit matching the challan details in the employer's statement. The employer must deposit the tax or correct the challan details.

body.title: The March exception
body.textWithBlank: TDS deducted from March salary must be deposited by 30 ___, not by the 7th of the next month.
body.explanation: For every other month the deadline is the 7th of the following month. March deductions get until 30 April.

body.title: Sneha's empty Q4
body.scenario: Sneha left a startup in Noida on 31 March 2026. Her Form 16 Part A shows receipt numbers for Q1 to Q3, but the Q4 row has no receipt number. Tax deducted in Q4 shows ₹52,000 and tax deposited shows ₹0. Her payslips for January to March show TDS deducted each month.
body.prompt: What does this tell Sneha, and what should she do before filing her return?
body.modelAnswer: The missing receipt number means the Q4 statement was not filed or was not processed, and ₹0 deposited means the tax cut from her salary has not reached the government against her PAN. Her Form 26AS will show ₹52,000 less than she actually had deducted. She should email the startup's HR or finance team with her payslips, asking them to deposit the tax if unpaid and file the Q4 statement, and to reissue Part A. Under section 401 (section 205), she cannot be made to pay tax that was already deducted from her salary. But if she files before the credit appears, her return may be processed with a demand she would then have to contest, so it is better to follow up first and keep all payslips as proof.

body.text: Under Form 130 from tax year 2026-27, the same information is still there but laid out differently: identity details sit in Part A, and the quarterly summary and deposit details sit in Part B. The checks in this lesson do not change.

points: Part A is generated through TRACES from your employer's quarterly TDS statements. It is the evidence of what reached your PAN.
Check three header fields first: your PAN, the employer's TAN and the assessment year.
Each quarter should show a receipt number, and tax deducted should equal tax deposited.
The challan table total, the quarterly summary total and your Form 26AS credit for that TAN must all agree.
Status F is final and matched. U and O need the employer to act.
Section 401 (section 205) protects you from paying tax already deducted, but get the employer to fix gaps before you file.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and reflects the rules as of September 2026. The receipt numbers, BSR codes and challan numbers shown are illustrative. For your specific situation, check TRACES and the e-filing portal or consult a chartered accountant.
